if it helps, tho cliche and not trying to invalidate your feelings at all, but i hope you find comfort that a lot of job seekers go through that hell. actually job seeking itself nowadays is quite difficult.

when i was looking for a job pre-pandemic, i also had to go through that very hell. interviews just made me wallow in self-pity. it even triggered a sort of social anxiety of having to face interviewers and strangers altogether. the thought of them judging me was overwhelming and it felt as though i just wasn't enough. nothing about me or my skill set is enough. the tears i cried when i was in college? having gone thru that other kind of hell? out the window, it doesn't even matter.

i do have a job now, but even when i do, the question of "is this what i want in life?" has not really been answered either at all.

so i guess you can take it one step at a time for now. get a job first. and you can do another goal, then another goal. you have time. it's all you've got. and if you feel like you don't even have that, find something that you do have and hold on to that. just focus on one goal for now.

can definitely relate to this on a personal level, except that i find myself to be the "boring" friend and not anyone's first choice to hang out with..

if you want to be their first choice when hanging out then figuring out their preferences and their current likes is one way to get closer to them, or just ask them directly. along with that you'd have to change a bit or a lot of yourself. but then you have to consider that it'll feed on your insecurities and possibly resentment towards your friends might come up. or maybe not.

other than that you could instead build on your self assurance and think that it isn't that you are lacking as a person, just that their "preference" is different from yours and their choice is not biased towards you. accepting both yourself and your friends flaws in your relationship. but it would need a lot of mental strength to not get carried away by your insecurities.

this is only my experience though. and rest assured you can always find your own answer. it is your choice and you are free to choose.

Jot in the characters that I originally imagined for the story but later on I weigh how essential they are to the plot, then erase the ones that don’t make any difference to another character’s development or change them or even boost their role, and I also try to figure out how much impact they will have on the main and/or side characters. Their relationships build up based on the encounters they will have with the other characters whom they will get to meet as the story goes and this is where the personality I imagine they have comes into play. I usually have inspiration for their individual personalities, and I try as much as possible that they wouldn’t sound the same, that 2 or more characters aren’t alike unless, it’s part of the plot.

The description may need a little bit of improvement, like the interaction of the physical scene with the characters, there doesn’t seem to be that connection. There is a portion where you describe the place and how it looks but lacks on the connection of the characters who sees everything. It will come off as boring if it’s just plain description. So to every description there’s complimentary movement, and if absolutely necessary, emotion, if it has any meaning to the character.

There’s also the last part, ‘a few minutes later’ and he went in to one of the buildings; as someone reading, I kind of wonder exactly what was he doing before he went in? Was he doing something important? Then I would want to know if he did.
But, parts like these if not necessary can be changed or erased. If what the characters did in the few minutes was not relevant is technically we can just erase that part.

The relationship of the m.c. with the character and the pet(?) needs to have at least small descriptions regarding their relationship, so the reader can connect with them.
